The prosecution case, in brief, is that five years ago, the complainant met the petitioner, who is her relative, at a function, and they shared their respective contact numbers.
After some days, they developed close relationship with each other.
It is alleged that the petitioner had taken some photos and videos from their Whatsapp call.
It is further alleged that, during the last Dussehra vacation, she had been to her uncle's house, and at that time, no one was present at the house.
At that time, the petitioner tried to keep physical relation with her.

4. The victim was 21 years old and the petitioner was 26 years old at the time of incident.

The statement of the victim has been recorded under Section 164 Cr.
P.C.
She, inter alia, stated that they were in a relationship.
However, the petitioner forcefully committed sexual intercourse with her.
He also asked the victim to send nude photographs of her, which he has taken screenshots and subsequently, it is alleged that the petitioner has been blackmailing the victim.

5. The petitioner had approached the learned Addl.
District & Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (Vigilance), Phulbani in BLAPL No.15/2024(T) praying for the grant of bail.

entities.text:
Addl.
District & Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (Vigilance), Phulbani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Court below vide its order dated 09.02.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has  Page 2 of 4  filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.
6. The petitioner has been in custody since 19.01.2024 .
It appears from the statement of the victim that they were in a relationship and it appears that the sexual act has been committed with consent.
Therefore, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

7. Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper,
including the following additional conditions:
(1) The petitioner shall not remain in contact with the victim in any manner whatsoever till the victim has been examined by the Court; and (2) He shall appear before the Court, without fail, on every date of hearing; and (3) He shall not influence any of the witnesses related to this case in any manner whatsoever.

In the event that the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge Subhasis Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack.
